sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page mate1260 and reference record 39834 (Z'graggen 1980)
sources.note: References for Matepi: Z'graggen 1980 (wordlist/overview), Pawley & Hammarström 2017, Pick 2020, Ethnologue 2025. No grammar, sketch or phonology; n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (DOI 10.15144/PL-D32; https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/144539)
sources.note: Matepi = language C26; ~300-item comparative list. Intro section 6 (pp. viii-ix) says the transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and for Matepi notes only s ~ z fluctuation and optional h. Stress is never mentioned; Matepi forms (e.g. mɛmu-, aita 'father'; ʌn, ɛnu- 'mother', printed p. 4) carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. (https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/handle/10125/73354)
sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for subclassification only. Zero occurrences of 'Matepi'; Mabuso mentioned only as a neighbouring group of Northern Adelbert. Says nothing about Matepi.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., entry 'Matepi' (Wayback capture 2017-02-02)
sources.note: 280 speakers (2003 SIL); Dialects 'None known'; related to the other Hanseman languages; no language resources listed apart from an OLAC link. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. (https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/252971)
sources.note: Classification and comparative tables with C26 Matepi forms (lɛvu 'arm', amu 'breast', garɛ...). Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. (https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/146484)
sources.note: Gazetteer: C26 Matepi, 238 speakers, villages Matepi and Autabak. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/146580)
sources.note: p. 6 (PDF p. 14): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' General remark for the whole survey. Matepi (MAT) is an 'additional member' of the Hanseman family 'included only in the population figures, but... disregarded in other respects' (p. 28 n. 9); section 2.21.12.23 (p. 30) gives villages Matepi, Autabak, Arar and notes 'Waugh (1924:94) collected a first word list.' No Matepi data, nothing on Matepi stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU. (https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/handle/1885/130077)
sources.note: pp. 13-14 (PDF p. 22): same sentence, stress marking omitted because stress patterning not yet established. p. 52: Waugh's Matepi-village wordlist provisionally assigned to Nake; no Matepi data.

sources.citation: ANU Open Research repository API search 'Matepi' (19 hits)
sources.note: Only Z'graggen's survey works (1969, 1970, 1971, 1975a, 1975b, 1976, 1980) and unrelated items; no description of Matepi.
360 lexical items, sole source Z'graggen 1980; forms carry r-tilde and vowel symbols but no stress marks; no phonology notes.
Stubs: classification (Matepi = North Gogol River subgroup with Utu-Silopi) and Ethnologue population only; no phonology, no stress.
